HomeEssentials Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer; and Casey Nguyen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the second quarter of 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:

1. Omnichannel initiatives progress. Our omnichannel efforts remain central to our strategy, turning our 1,200 brick-and-mortar stores into efficient fulfillment centers that integrate digital and physical channels. This approach is fueling revenue growth, improving margins, and building customer loyalty against online-only competitors like Amazon. In Q2, omnichannel sales—including BOPIS, curbside pickup, ship-from-store, and in-store returns of online orders—hit $285 million, or 28% of total digital sales, up 32% year-over-year. This exceeded our 25-30% growth target and beat the National Retail Federation's industry average of 22%. BOPIS drove $175 million, up 38% with 1.2 million orders, a 42% volume increase. Curbside, now in 95% of stores post-2023 rollout, added $92 million, up 29%, handling 15% of digital apparel and home goods. Omnichannel penetration reached 12% of total sales, up from 8%, nearing Target's 14%. BOPIS same-day fulfillment was 98.5%, powered by our StoreHub platform. BOPIS average order value was $145, 22% above pure e-commerce's $119, with 65% of customers adding impulse items, up 18%. We've rolled out AI Dynamic Inventory Engine with Manhattan Associates and Google Cloud, cutting BOPIS stockouts 35% to 7.8% and boosting app downloads 24% to 4.2 million users. Micro-fulfillment pilots in 50 Northeast stores using Locus Robotics cut labor 40%. Sunbelt regions—420 stores in Florida, Texas, Carolinas—saw 45% BOPIS growth; curbside at 22% penetration. Midwest ship-from-store up 26%; Northeast BOPIS AOV up 28% on premium items like Threshold. Margins expanded 210 bps to 42.5%, saving $8-12 shipping per order. Omnichannel CLV is 2.7x higher, 68% repeat rate, 41% loyalty conversion. We're targeting 35% penetration by FY2025 with $150 million CapEx, RFID in 600 stores, BOPIS+, same-hour curbside, and drone pilots. This delivers a moat in the $1.2 trillion market.

2. Impact of shrink/theft on gross margin. Shrink continues as a headwind, but our initiatives are countering it. Gross margin rose 10 bps to 28.4%, our best Q2 in three years, thanks to private-label mix at 42% up from 38%, sourcing from Vietnam/Bangladesh, and markdowns down 15 bps with turns at 5.8x. Shrink cost 125 bps, up from 95 bps, at 1.75% of sales or $49 million—matching NRF's 1.6% average with 12% ORC rise. External theft 55% or 0.96%, up from 0.72%, led by electronics/beauty at $45/incident. Internal 25% or 0.44%, up from scan avoidance. Northeast 2.3% shrink on ORC like Levi's/Dyson; California 2.1% post-Prop 47; Midwest/Southeast 1.2-1.4%. Countermeasures: Eversee AI in 65% stores flagged 28,000 events at 92% accuracy; RFID on 75% apparel cut unknown shrink 18%; self-checkout validation down avoidance 35%. Expect 1.6% shrink H2, 110 bps impact, with $45 million CapEx on Genetec AI. RILA task force advocacy, ShrinkSmart training cut internal 12%. Reclaiming 50 bps unlocks $14 million EBITDA.

3. Comparable store sales growth (YoY). Comps grew 4.2%, excluding 12 openings/3 closures, beating 2-4% guidance and 3.5% consensus—sixth straight positive quarter, 8.7% two-year stack. Traffic +2.8% via Store Pulse AI; AUR +1.1% on premium Forge Collection; units +0.3% to 2.8. Apparel +6.1% with 18% BOPIS; footwear +1.2%; home -0.8% offset by 42% private-label. Southeast/Midwest +6.4%/+5.2% post-150 NextGen remodels; West +1.9%; Canada flat. $45 million supply chain for same-day curbside on 65% SKUs; inventory 8 weeks. Q3/FY comps 3-5%.

4. Labor costs and store payroll leverage. Store payroll 65% of labor, at 9.4% of sales, down 70 bps YoY on 4.2% comps. SPLH +5.8% to $185; payroll $285 million up 1.8%. MaxShift AI in 82% stores cut overstaffing 12%; self-checkout in 650 stores at 42% transactions. Wages +3.8% to $18.25; MaxPerformance bonuses, 68% retention. Sunbelt 8.7%; West 10.8%; Midwest/Northeast 9.1%. NPS 72 correlates to 4% comp lift; 50-75 bps more deleverage FY24.

5. Strategies for inventory optimization. DIO down 22% to 52 days, aiding 180 bps margin to 38.2%. AI with IBM Watson 89% SKU accuracy; VMI 65% SKUs cut excess 18%/$220 million. RFID 95%, ship-from-store 22% digital; GMROI 4.2x. Southeast/Midwest 48 days; omnichannel turns 6.8x. Trim slow-movers to 8%; blockchain Q1 2024. Unlocked $350 million capital.

6. Digital marketing effectiveness. Spend $42.7 million at 4.2% revenue, ROAS 6.8x, CAC $18.42. Google 7.9x, geofencing +42% visits/$112 million; Meta 5.6x; SEO +24% traffic; email $4.20/$1. Sunbelt 7.4x; CDP AI lookalikes; CTV pilots Q4. $1.2 billion attributable revenue next year.

7. Inventory levels (YoY). Inventory $1.15 billion, down 8.2% from $1.25 billion—sixth straight decline. Apparel/softlines -11.5%/$420 million; hardlines -4.8%/$380 million; consumables flat/$350 million. Turns 5.8x, DIO 63 days; markdowns 18%. Midwest/Southeast -10%; Northeast/West -6%. AI Manhattan 92% accuracy; RFID 75%; VMI 40%. Q4 down 5-6%.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more details on our financial results.

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the second quarter of 2024.

Total revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

Gross margin was 38.4%, primarily driven by private-label mix shift, omnichannel efficiencies, lower markdowns, and shrink mitigation efforts.

Operating expenses were $2.3 billion, representing 82% of revenue.

Net income was $140 million, or $1.02 per share.

We generated $300 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently $1.15 billion, down 8.2% year-over-year.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Taylor Kim, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Morgan Patel to discuss store operations, and then Casey Nguyen to discuss marketing initiatives.

Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our Threshold premium bedding and decor line, which has seen strong uptake with 55% of online orders fulfilled via BOPIS and solid sell-through in stores. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in sustainable apparel.

Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented NextGen remodels in 150 locations, incorporating RFID for 99% availability and experiential zones, and are seeing 7-10% comp lifts in early quarters.

Casey Nguyen, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Morgan. Our new Flash Finds campaign has increased brand awareness by 25%, driving traffic through targeted pop-ups and digital tie-ins.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of organized retail crime on your sales?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Good question, John. As we detailed, ORC contributed significantly to the 1.75% shrink rate, particularly in urban Northeast and California stores with smash-and-grabs and bulk thefts in electronics and apparel. It's a 125 bps gross margin headwind, but our AI vision systems, RFID expansion, and partnerships have reduced incidents and positioned us to moderate to 1.6% in H2.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Emily. We're guiding to 3% to 5% comps for Q3, with upside into Q4 holidays. This factors in continued traffic from omnichannel, value assortment strength, and remodel benefits, while monitoring inflation on middle-income wallets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez (Bank of America):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Mike. Our strategies include AI demand forecasting at 89-92% accuracy, VMI with key vendors shifting $150-220 million risk upstream, and RFID/automation for real-time visibility. Micro-fulfillment and dual-sourcing mitigated Red Sea issues, cutting DIO to 52-63 days and boosting turns to 5.8-6.8x in key areas.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Great to hear, Lisa. Omnichannel shoppers show 41% loyalty conversion versus 29% online-only, with 68% repeat rates and 2.7x CLV. Penetration at 92% supports resilience, driving basket building and retention amid comp growth.

Operator:

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
